title: Just put it in my logbook
topic: Probity in training, research, audit and applications
stem:
You are an F2 doctor. Dr Hughes, another F2, is applying for core surgical training and needs more logged procedures. She asks you to confirm in her e-logbook that she performed a skin lesion excision last week.

You were there, but she observed while you did the procedure.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Explain that you can't confirm she performed it, as she observed.
options.brief: The logbook must reflect what she actually did.
options.detailed: Logbooks are used to judge applicants' experience. Confirming she performed a procedure she observed would be dishonest.

options.text: Suggest she logs it accurately, as observed.
options.brief: Logbooks usually record observed procedures too.
options.detailed: Many logbooks have a category for procedures observed or assisted. Logging it accurately still shows her interest and experience.

options.text: Confirm it, as she has done similar procedures before.
options.brief: Previous experience doesn't change what happened in this case.
options.detailed: She may be competent, which makes this tempting, but the record would still be false.

options.text: Offer to help her find chances to do it under supervision.
options.detailed: Supporting her to gain real experience helps her application honestly, and is a constructive response to her request.

options.text: Confirm it as 'assisted', as a compromise.
options.detailed: This feels like a middle ground, but she observed, so it would still be inaccurate.

options.text: Report her to the training programme director for asking.
options.brief: Disproportionate for a request you can simply decline.
options.detailed: Repeated attempts to falsify records would need reporting, but a single request is best dealt with by declining and explaining.

options.text: Tell other colleagues that she asked you to falsify her logbook.
options.detailed: This would damage her reputation and doesn't address the issue.
A one-off doesn't make a false record acceptable.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you maintain honesty in training records when a colleague asks for help with her application.
explanation.keyDetails: She observed the procedure. The logbook will be used for her application. You are being asked to confirm it.
explanation.reasoning: [A] keeps the record honest, [B] suggests an accurate alternative, and [D] supports her honestly. The distractors falsify the record ([C], [E], [H]), or respond disproportionately or unprofessionally ([F], [G]).
explanation.competing: [E] is the tempting distractor, as it seems a compromise, but it's still inaccurate.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 4, honesty in records and applications.
